claims.statement: At fixed b in (0,1), the unit-volume correlation on total deficit two is exactly (1/b) times the pairwise power factor and the flat-area integral.
hypotheses: Distinct marked points; 0 < mu_i < 1; sum mu_i = 2; gamma=2b and KRV charge beta_i=mu_i/b.
The GMC first moment uses the source reference measure |w|_+^(-4) d^2w.
claims.scope_limit: The correlation itself is not the complex-hyperbolic volume density.

claims.statement: The curvature-minus-one form is -2i times the area-logarithm Hessian; the pairwise factors are pluriharmonic off collisions.
hypotheses: A local holomorphic normalization of the developing differential; noncolliding configurations.
claims.scope_limit: The top exterior power, not the raw correlation, gives the volume. Collision delta terms are excluded from the open moduli chart.

claims.statement: Strict extended Seiberg inequalities hold at s=-1, and KRV charge analyticity gives the simple residue; changing from s to t=b(s+1) changes its coefficient by b.
hypotheses: Fixed b in (0,1); fixed distinct insertion positions; a charge neighborhood inside the strict moment inequalities.
claims.scope_limit: This is charge continuation of the probabilistic/unit-volume expression, not a spectral-tail bound or a b-uniform limit.

claims.statement: The one-screening integrands are the flat developing periods after the stated charge substitution.
claims.scope_limit: Twisted-cycle or branch conventions must be retained; an arbitrary real arc is not a global single-valued block.

claims.statement: Fixing 0,1,z,infinity gives the stated area integral; equal-half weights give half the torus period area and the upper-half-plane density of labeled volume 2pi.
hypotheses: The elliptic K notation uses the parameter, not modulus, convention.
Curvature is -1 and labels are retained.
claims.scope_limit: No quotient by a permutation group and no cusp-WP normalization is implicit.

claims.statement: Heusener-Porti torsion disintegrates into the Goldman top power and peripheral forms; all three rescale together when B is rescaled.
hypotheses: Good, boundary-regular SL2(C) representation of an n-holed sphere.
B -> lambda^2 B, omega -> lambda^2 omega, nu_i -> lambda nu_i, Omega -> lambda^(2d+n) Omega; a common complex square-root choice is used.
claims.scope_limit: The coefficient sqrt(2) in nu_i is specific to B=-tr. Pulling the unrestricted top form directly to a fixed-trace leaf gives zero.

claims.statement: The consistently WP-calibrated relative density has the local rescaled CH limit on controlled positive-area families.
hypotheses: Cone openings in (0,2pi); a local geometric holonomy component; the positive trace-coordinate density fixes the orientation.
Global marked holonomy injectivity is used only when every opening is at most pi.
claims.scope_limit: Neither a global character-variety identification nor an unrescaled Euclidean Goldman measure is asserted.

claims.statement: The equal-trace Fricke blowup yields the Heron quadric and the displayed first correction to the WP density.
hypotheses: a=-2sin(A/8); x,y,z=-2-A(X,Y,Z); chart u>0,v>0; positive density orientation.
claims.scope_limit: A local compact-chart expansion in blown-up character coordinates; its first correction cannot be integrated termwise over the cusp.

claims.statement: A branchwise half-density WKB kernel gives the Liouville measure at leading order with the displayed 2pi*hbar normalization.
hypotheses: One nondegenerate phase branch and the specified normalization, spectral measure and polarization.
claims.scope_limit: Multiple-branch interference and elliptic continuation are not established by this conditional calculation.

claims.statement: The length/charge dictionary, unshifted versus pure-heavy openings, and s=A/(4pi b^2)-1 distinguish the first-moment locus from the joint semiclassical regime.
hypotheses: TV alpha=Q/2+i*ell/(4pi b); actual hyperbolic area uses 2pi(sum deficits-2).
claims.scope_limit: The auxiliary tetrahedral angle Gram matrix is not automatically a compact geometric tetrahedron; fixed-b residue and A proportional to b^(4/3) are different limits.

claims.statement: The real weight domain, transverse residue coordinate and exponent differences are fixed explicitly.
hypotheses: 0<b<1; 0<mu_i<1; sum mu_i=2; fields at 0,1,z,infinity.
claims.scope_limit: Complex charge continuation keeps both chiral factors analytic rather than conjugating charge variables.

claims.statement: A continued infinite spectral derivation requires a specified residue-retaining path, locally fixed tails and locally uniform integrable majorants.
hypotheses: Finite pinches and any extra discrete terms are separated; the regular remainder is holomorphic through epsilon=0.
Contours coincide with Q/2+iR outside a fixed compact set, or connecting integrals vanish uniformly.
claims.scope_limit: No required majorant is proved here. The initial bootstrap theorem does not cover the one-screening locus and does not itself justify this continuation. No uniform b->0 or extra coalescence estimate is claimed.

claims.statement: Finite DOZZ residue algebra gives two channels and their coefficients; the resulting residue identity also follows independently from the first moment and period area.
hypotheses: Generic noncoincident weights first; sum-coordinate residues; reflection partners and the unfolded-contour factor are retained.
claims.scope_limit: The infinite-contour proof is conditional on s13.spectral_continuation; the first-moment/period proof is not. These are two different routes to the same finite formula.

claims.statement: Euler periods times the common charge factor are the normalized one-screening Virasoro blocks via weight-one screening Ward identities.
hypotheses: Branches positive on (0,1), continued to C minus ((-infinity,0] union [1,infinity)).
Closed twisted/Pochhammer cycles justify the Ward argument; internal weights are positive at c>25.
claims.scope_limit: This does not give a second-order equation for arbitrary four-point blocks; the second ordinary period coalesces at a balanced exponent.

claims.statement: Gauss connection formulas give the Gamma matrix, determinant -delta0/delta1 and the beta-rescaled sine matrix.
hypotheses: delta0*delta1 is nonzero for both displayed pairs to be bases; the same branch chart and ordering are used.
claims.scope_limit: A balanced specialization requires a logarithmic basis, not entrywise substitution into the singular matrix.

claims.statement: The complex beta integral fixes one diagonal area coefficient and monodromy at the other puncture fixes the second; Gamma reflection gives the stated indefinite Hermitian pairing and its congruence.
hypotheses: For the beta integral, 0<p,q<1 and p+q>1.
First delta0*delta1 != 0; continuity at delta1=0 keeps delta0 != 0 and uses a uniform local integral dominator.
claims.scope_limit: The signature is (1,1), so the two terms are not positive probability channels. This proof needs no infinite spectral integration.

claims.statement: The two-dimensional Hermitian determinant identity and hypergeometric Wronskian yield the positive curvature-minus-one density.
hypotheses: The area is positive on the period line; x=Re z,y=Im z; d^2z=dx dy.
claims.scope_limit: Finite formulas and their local derivatives do not certify any quantum spectral tail.

claims.statement: Collision cone angles 2pi|delta_nu| and balanced cusps give the labeled Gauss-Bonnet volume 2pi(1-sum|delta_nu|)=4pi min_i(mu_i,1-mu_i).
hypotheses: Curvature -1; three labeled four-point boundary partitions; balanced ends treated as cusps.
claims.scope_limit: No integration of a nonuniform character-coordinate correction is used.

claims.statement: At four equal half-weights, the logarithmic basis, finite involution, indefinite area form, Gamma(2) monodromy and explicit cusp density arise from the elliptic/logarithmic limit.
hypotheses: K uses parameter z; L=log(16); counterclockwise puncture loops and oriented periods Omega1=4K(z),Omega2=4iK(1-z).
claims.scope_limit: The second solution is a logarithmic/parameter-derivative block, not a second independent ordinary block of the same weight. Numerical convergence in weights would not establish spectral coalescence bounds.

claims.statement: TV normalization uses the displayed double-Gamma/trivalent factors, reflected infinity charge and square roots of both Plancherel factors.
hypotheses: External ordering (alpha1,alpha3,alpha2,Q-alpha4); square-root branches inherited by continuation.
claims.scope_limit: Principal-contour normalization identities do not alone establish the full continued infinite operator at the screened locus.

claims.statement: The double-Gamma shift reduces each screened trivalent product to a common b-dependent scalar times ordinary Gamma factors, giving the finite sine matrix and rescaled pairing.
hypotheses: Generic real nonbalanced weights; common scalar K_b removed consistently.
claims.scope_limit: This is an exactly normalized finite period operator. Identifying it with the residue of the infinite TV operator still requires s13.spectral_continuation; it is not a bare Barnes integral value.

claims.statement: Local pinch regularization fixes analytic square roots and the complex-orthogonal or real-indefinite normalized finite matrix.
hypotheses: alpha_s=s_j+epsilon*xi with xi != 0,-1; generic auxiliary factors; a common infinity reflection factor is canceled.
claims.scope_limit: Analytic square roots and absolute square roots give different pairings. Balanced limits require the logarithmic basis.

claims.statement: Double-sine shifts give the analytically continued sine product, oscillation in small real b and vanishing at balanced weights.
claims.scope_limit: Division of a finite operator by pointwise Plancherel values does not define a limiting bare symbol.

claims.statement: The reflected screening Gram family has a rank-two planar limit, two exactly zero principal cofactors and explicit negative off-diagonal cofactor for fixed interior weights and sufficiently small positive h.
hypotheses: theta_i=pi*mu_i, sum theta_i=2pi, h=2pi*b^2; the specified outward-normal angle Gram convention is retained.
claims.scope_limit: The formal angle matrix is not an existence assertion. Lorentzian signature alone does not imply an ordinary convex hyperbolic tetrahedron; this family cannot have a nondegenerate shrinking compact rank-three limit.

claims.statement: At b=0 the reflected screening potential cancels to four dilogarithms and its reduced saddle equation has no nonzero regular solution when both exponent differences are nonzero.
hypotheses: P=exp(2pi i delta0),R=exp(2pi i delta1); consistent branches; canceled dilogarithm branch factors excluded.
claims.scope_limit: An apparent double branch root before cancellation is not a regular classical fold. Balanced P=1 or R=1 makes the reduced potential constant on a consistent branch.

claims.statement: The genuine regular compact family has edge-dihedral charges, a rank-three Euclidean Gram limit and the displayed area, angle and volume Taylor coefficients.
hypotheses: Six equal actual interior edge dihedrals; ell tends to zero; W(0)=0; dW=-3 ell d eta.
claims.scope_limit: Intrinsic cone deficits and edge dihedrals encode different data; these charges are not the reflected screened labels.

claims.statement: Exact polynomial factorization and local derivatives at the regular Euclidean root give a nondegenerate cubic classical fold and zeta=6sqrt(2)t/h^(2/3).
hypotheses: a_E=(1+2sqrt(2)i)/3; u_E=a_E^(-5); h=2pi b^2; local dilogarithm branches fixed away from branch divisors.
claims.scope_limit: A local classical normal form and its scale do not prove a uniform quantum integral asymptotic or specify its global contour.

hypotheses: The source geometric root and branch choices for compact tetrahedra; the v-independent scalar convention is retained.
claims.scope_limit: This normalizes the classical volume action; it does not choose or justify the complete quantum contour contribution.

claims.statement: The equal-label exact TV integrand and shift quotient fix u=exp(2pi i b w), and the correct saddle lift keeps the three argument types inside the fundamental strip at small b.
